subjects.name: Data Structures and Algorithms

Typical running time over the distribution of expected inputs.

Running time for the most favorable input of a given size.

Extra information stored beyond the actual data values.

subjects.name: System Design
defs: A logical grouping of instances that share similar characteristics and are managed together for scaling.
Automatic launching or terminating of instances based on user-defined policies, schedules, and health checks.
A condition where a user-set threshold is passed, possibly triggering a scaling activity.
The amount of available compute size at a given time within defined minimum and maximum values.
The time Auto Scaling waits before allowing another scaling change from an alarm.
The time it takes to return a response to a request.
A value below which a given percentage of observations in a distribution fall.
Removing instances from an existing Auto Scaling group.
Adding instances to an existing Auto Scaling group.
A process that changes the size, configuration, or makeup of an Auto Scaling group.
A description of how Auto Scaling scales a group in response to changing demand.
The latency experienced by the slowest requests in the long tail of a distribution.
The automatic restricting or slowing down of a process based on one or more limits.
The rate at which a service processes requests, typically measured in requests per second.
A high availability strategy where a workload runs simultaneously in multiple regions and serves traffic from all.
A disaster recovery strategy involving a primary region and a standby region.
The fraction of time a service is usable, measured by successful requests over total.
A distinct location within a region that is insulated from failures in other zones.
A disaster recovery strategy copying backups from a primary region to a standby region for restoration.
The likelihood that data will be retained over a long period of time.
A data center that a service uses to perform service-specific operations closer to users.
The rate at which service level objectives may be missed within a period.
A call that checks the health status of each instance in an Auto Scaling group.
An active-passive strategy where the workload is fully scaled in both primary and standby regions.
An active-passive strategy replicating data to a standby and provisioning only core infrastructure.
A named set of resources in the same geographical area, comprised of at least three Availability Zones.
An explicit or implicit contract with users including consequences of meeting or missing objectives.
A carefully defined quantitative measure of some aspect of the level of service provided.
A target value or range of values for a service level measured by an indicator.
An active-passive strategy where the workload is scaled down in the passive standby region but functional.
The method a service uses to achieve high availability, such as replicating data across servers.
A solution for replicating data across different regions in near-real time.
A concept where data written successfully is updated in all copies across all regions over time.

A read returning data from one region that might not show the most recent write.
A concept where data written successfully updates all copies in all regions.
An active-active strategy where reads and writes occur in the originating region and replicate synchronously.
An active-active strategy where writes go to one primary region and reads are served from the originating region.
An active copy of a database instance receiving replicated updates from the source.
A read returning the most up-to-date data reflecting all previous successful writes.
An index with a partition key and sort key that can differ from the table and span all partitions.

A simple primary key composed of one attribute used to distribute data.
A partition of data in an index split into primary and replica shards.
An attribute used to sort partition keys in a composite primary key.

A fixed-size chunk of secure network-attached memory running a cache service.
A web service speeding distribution of web content via a worldwide network of data centers.
A sequence of messages or jobs held in temporary storage awaiting transmission or processing.
A web address that uniquely identifies a queue.
A communication channel for sending messages and subscribing to notifications.
The period a message stays invisible after a component receives it from a queue.
An item watching a metric over time and triggering actions when thresholds are crossed.
Monitoring of provided metrics derived at a five-minute frequency.
A deployment method replacing original instances with a separate replacement environment.
A standard unit of software containing application code and all relevant dependencies.
A practice where code changes are automatically built, tested, and prepared for release.
A practice where developers regularly merge code changes and automated builds and tests run.
Monitoring of provided metrics derived at a one-minute frequency.

A replica set member that replicates the primary's data.
